extracted.intended_audience: newsroom leaders, audience development editors, data analysts, and journalists interested in using analytics to guide editorial strategy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for designing, using, and governing analytics tailored to newsroom editorial priorities so they inform both daily editorial choices and longer-term strategy. Emphasizes culture, tooling, metrics design, platform-awareness, and the balance between data and editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored to specific editorial priorities and organizational imperatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial analytics are tailored to the specific editorial priorities and organizational imperatives of a given organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doing analytics well requires knowing what you are trying to do editorially (who you are trying to reach, where, and with what?) and what you need to do organizationally to do this (do you live off advertising? subscriptions? donations?). Avoid one-size-fits-all, off-the-shelf approaches that don't reflect editorial goals or business model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform both short-term and long-term decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial analytics are used to inform both short-term day-to-day decisions and longer-term strategic development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term optimization (making sure stories find readers and readers find stories) is important, but analytics should also support better use of newsroom resources and the development of new editorial products and areas of emphasis. Do not restrict analytics to immediate traffic boosts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continually evolve with the changing media environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial analytics continually evolve to keep pace with a changing media environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-site homepage traffic remains useful, but analytics must equip newsrooms to understand mobile users and off-site use on social media platforms. Metrics and tools should be reviewed and updated as platforms and user behavior change; static metrics risk 'flying blind.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sense of numbers and act on insights (actionability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best-practice analytics know how to make sense of numbers and act on those insights rather than just display them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on actionable information: analysis should lead to concrete editorial actions (reorganizing desks, changing workflows, launching products). Anti-pattern: having big screens with numbers that go up and down but no interpretation or follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratize data with user-friendly interfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop user-friendly interfaces that can help 'democratize' data across the newsroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools and dashboards (e.g., The Guardian’s Ophan) should allow rank-and-file journalists and senior editors alike to understand metrics. Usability and clear presentation increase uptake and informed decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop clear indicators of success aligned with editorial goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Create clear indicators for what the organization considers success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design metrics that reflect editorial priorities (example: Die Welt’s 'article score'). Indicators should be meaningful to editorial teams and tied to the newsroom’s mission rather than generic traffic statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to use analytics to make editorial changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial organizations must be willing to actually use insights from analytics to make editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include reorganizing the newsroom (Financial Times) and launching new editorial products (The Economist). Analytics without willingness to change practices and structures is ineffective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture of data: journalist engagement and literacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Good analytics is as much about organization and culture as about tools and technology — journalists need to be involved and literate in data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a culture of data where journalists at all levels know how to make sense of numbers and act on them. If journalists don't engage, metrics will be shaped primarily by advertising/commercial/technological priorities, not editorial needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance analytics with editorial judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytics should complement editorial judgment; data never tells the full story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use quantitative audience data to inform but not replace editorial decision-making. Guard against the 'tyranny of numbers' by combining data with qualitative judgment and editorial values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and manage data-quality and access limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial analytics must recognize that data and tools have quality and access issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about limitations: data never tells the full story, and even the best systems face data-quality and access constraints. Build processes to validate and contextualize metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid narrow focus on short-term engagement metrics and surface-level tweaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytics should be about more than short-term optimization of pageviews and unique users via headline/placement/picture tweaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let analytics be reduced to chasing clicks through superficial changes. Metrics should include measures that reflect deeper editorial success and audience relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be platform-aware: measure beyond on-site homepage traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytics should account for platform-specific behavior (mobile, social, off-site) rather than rely solely on on-site homepage metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure analytics capture where audiences actually consume content (mobile apps, social platforms, aggregation), or you risk incomplete understanding of reach and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate resources and design strategy, not just acquire tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Sophisticated analytics is about how resources are allocated and organizational design, not simply newsroom size or tool procurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small startups (Quartz, De Correspondent, Ze.tt) can outpace legacy organizations if they allocate resources and structure teams to prioritize analytics. Investment decisions should focus on people, processes, and alignment with editorial goals as much as on technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align metrics and analytics with the business model
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytics strategies should reflect the organization's business model (advertising, subscriptions, donations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different revenue models imply different editorial priorities and success indicators; metrics should be chosen and interpreted in light of how the organization sustains itself.
